bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material price inflation (steel) with pass-through lags; Slower-than-expected EV adoption rates; Customer concentration (Top 10 = 70%); Transitional dependency on demerged Industrial entity for traded goods.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic on volume growth but defensive on margin compression; committed to transparency post-feedback; emphasizes 'quality of earnings' and cash flow over pure top-line growth.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Reverse carve-out structure: SKF India Ltd retained Auto business while Industrial demerged; currently renting land/assets to Industrial entity; high traded goods volume is temporary bridge until new auto-capacity comes online; EV bearings command multifold pricing despite lower unit count.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: OEM contributes ~66% of sales (+20% YoY); Distribution ~20% (slight decline); Exports ~8%; Industrial share ~6%. 2-Wheeler is dominant volume contributor. Top 5 customers ~50%, Top 10 ~70% (Bajaj, Mahindra, Tata key).

latest_quarter.body: Margin compression due to OEM mix shift (lower margin vs aftermarket), raw material inflation (steel) with lagged pass-through, and transitional trading from Industrial entity. Sustainable PBT guided at 11-12%.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 6-8% CAGR expected; Margin: Sustainable PBT margin of 11-12% in near term (FY27); Order Inflow: Strong wins in EV motors and wheel hubs; Capex: INR 200cr in FY27, part of INR 500cr plan (FY26-28).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Strong portfolio of wins across 2W, PV, CV extending to 2030; Specific new launches in EV motor bearings and wheel hub bearings for FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: White spaces in unitized bearings for SCV/LCV and low-friction transmissions for CAFE-3 norms; EV adoption (currently 6% of 2W, 4% of PV) offering higher value-per-product despite lower bearing count.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: SKF India posted 14.8% YoY revenue growth in Q4FY26 driven by strong OEM volumes, but PBT margins compressed to ~9% due to lapping of Q3 one-off gains and transitional demerger costs. Management guides for a sustainable 11-12% PBT margin in FY27 as capacity expansions (INR 500cr plan) reduce reliance on traded goods from the demerged industrial entity.

open.horizon: on shareholder approval at the 65th AGM, 14th August 2026
open.item: The Board has recommended a final dividend of INR 40 per equity share of face value INR 10 each for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the 65th AGM on 14th August 2026, with a record date of 3rd July 2026.

The Company intends to reach net zero by 2050, acting beyond its factories by driving supplier decarbonisation with low-carbon steel and renewables and cutting logistics emissions through smarter lanes, CNG vehicles and reduced air freight.

The Company is working towards net zero by 2050, including supplier decarbonisation with low-carbon steel and renewables and lower logistics emissions through smarter lanes, CNG vehicles and reduced air freight.
The Company is committed to achieving zero accidents across all SKF operations and reported an improvement versus the previous year.
Through optimised consumption, scaling reuse and improved recharge, the Company's sites are advancing water neutrality, aiming to return more to the environment than they consume.
The Company is expanding capabilities across EV powertrains, unitized wheel-end systems and sensor-integrated solutions, describing the EV space as its strongest momentum.

The Company is rebalancing its automotive portfolio and sharpening focus on high-growth opportunities, particularly the two-wheeler segment, with the Bengaluru Technical Centre as a dedicated R&D and manufacturing-excellence hub.

Following the FY 2025-26 demerger, SKF Automotive will concentrate on supporting India's evolving mobility ecosystem across EV, two-wheeler and wheel-end bearings segments while leveraging SKF's global technology ecosystem.

SKF Automotive will concentrate on supporting India's evolving mobility ecosystem across EV, two-wheeler and wheel-end bearings segments, operating with strategic autonomy while leveraging SKF's global technology ecosystem.

Each of the Company's three facilities - Pune, Bengaluru and Haridwar - is described as part of the investment programme being built for the years ahead, with Haridwar specifically included in the post-demerger investment.

The manufacturing strategy lists capacity building for high-growth segments, regionalisation and localisation, technology step-up and assortment portfolio rationalisation (Factory PLP) as stated priorities.
The Company is advancing towards Industry 4.0 through IIoT-enabled systems, integrated Manufacturing Execution Systems and AI-based analytics to enable predictive maintenance and consistent quality.

risks.note: Global disruptions, trade restrictions and regional instability may affect supply chain continuity and input cost stability; mitigated through localisation, dual sourcing, inventory optimisation, digital supply chain solutions and a more regionalised operating model. The MD&A separately flags Middle East / Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea disruption, US-China tariff and technology restrictions, and volatile energy markets as pressures on an energy-importing economy such as India.

Fluctuations in raw material prices, energy costs and logistics expenses may impact profitability and operational planning; managed through pricing strategies, productivity improvement, cost optimisation programmes and flexible sourcing models.

As digitalisation accelerates, exposure to cybersecurity threats and data protection requirements has increased; addressed through investment in IT security infrastructure, employee awareness programmes and periodic security audits aligned with Group-wide data protection standards. A cybersecurity and data privacy framework and policy are in place, and no data privacy or cybersecurity consumer complaints were received in FY 2025-26 or the prior year.

Rapid advancements and evolving business models require continuous innovation to remain relevant; the Company leverages the SKF Group's Technology Radar, open innovation platforms and sustained R&D investment.

Growing expectations for seamless customer experiences and integrated digital operations are accelerating digital transformation; addressed through strategic investment in digital capabilities, IT landscape simplification and targeted hiring of digital talent.

Access to skilled talent in critical domains remains essential for sustaining innovation and operational excellence; addressed through leadership development, employee engagement, diversity and inclusion and strategic talent acquisition supporting succession planning.

Climate change, water scarcity and evolving environmental regulations present operational and reputational exposure (the risk description is truncated in the source); the Company is advancing water neutrality initiatives, decarbonisation targets, renewable energy adoption and climate scenario risk assessments to prepare for future regulatory and environmental challenges.

Following the demerger of the industrial business, the reporting boundary changed: intensity ratios and prior-year comparatives are not directly comparable, and MSME sourcing fell from 43% to 39% and district / neighbouring-district sourcing from 86.59% to 79% because previous-year figures included the subsequently demerged entity.
